questions.q: The word ‘pedagogy’ has been derived from the ____ word “pedagogue”.
questions.explanation: Pedagogy comes from the Greek paidagogos (pais, child + agogos, leader), originally the person who led children to school. It is not of Latin origin.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is not true about pedagogy?
options: It is a method or way of teaching
It is derived from the Greek word “pedagogue”
It helps a teacher understand how learning should be facilitated.
It harms the quality of teaching and learning.
questions.explanation: Pedagogy is the method and practice of teaching; it derives from Greek and guides how teachers facilitate learning. Good pedagogy improves, rather than harms, the quality of teaching and learning.

questions.q: Pedagogy can enhance the student-teacher relationship.
questions.explanation: A well-chosen pedagogy builds understanding, engagement and communication between teacher and students, thereby strengthening the student-teacher relationship.

questions.q: ____ learning is based on the model that knowledge can be created within a population where members actively interact by sharing experiences and take on asymmetry roles.
questions.explanation: Collaborative learning holds that knowledge is co-created within a group whose members interact, share experiences and take on different (asymmetric) roles. Constructivism is broader and need not involve group interaction.

questions.q: The Pedagogical Model provides an overview of the learning cycle and breaks it down into ____ domains or phases of instruction.
questions.explanation: As taught in the lecture, the Pedagogical Model divides the learning cycle into five domains or phases of instruction (commonly listed as engage, explore, explain, elaborate and evaluate).

questions.q: Which of the following is not a type of inquiry-based approach?
questions.explanation: The recognised levels of inquiry-based learning are confirmation, structured, guided and open inquiry. 'Confrontation' is a distractor resembling 'confirmation' and is not one of them.

questions.q: In experiential learning, students are engaged ____.
questions.explanation: Experiential learning involves the whole person, engaging learners intellectually, emotionally (soulfully), socially and physically through direct experience and reflection.

questions.q: ____ stage of experiential theory by Kolb focuses on planning.
questions.explanation: In Kolb's cycle, active experimentation is where learners plan and try out what they have learned in new situations. Abstract conceptualization is about forming concepts and conclusions, not planning action.

questions.q: People with a ____ learning style can often act on “gut feeling” and will rely on others' analysis rather than their own.
questions.explanation: Kolb's accommodating (doing and feeling) style is hands-on and intuitive; such learners act on gut feeling and lean on others' analysis. Assimilators, by contrast, prefer careful logical analysis of their own.

questions.q: According to the ____ principle, students learn better from animation and narration than from animation and on-screen text.
questions.explanation: Mayer's modality principle states that presenting words as spoken narration rather than on-screen text with graphics reduces visual overload by using both auditory and visual channels. The multimedia principle concerns words plus pictures versus words alone.
